analysis.investment_thesis: B.R.Goyal passes several of my quantitative filters — P/E 8.44, P/B ~1.1, D/E ~0.31, and price below my Graham Number estimate (~INR 170) — which is rare for a recently-listed name. However, negative operating cash flow (-INR 36 Cr) and FCF (-INR 58 Cr) in FY2025, combined with a short public track record, deny the margin of safety I require for a conviction buy.
key_strengths: P/E of 8.44 and P/B ~1.1 — within my strict value thresholds.
Low leverage: Borrowings INR 77 Cr vs Equity INR 245 Cr (D/E 0.31).
Six consecutive years of positive earnings; net profit CAGR 25.6%.
key_risks: Operating CF swung to -INR 36 Cr in FY2025 — working capital bloat typical of contractors.
Recent IPO (equity doubled from 127→245 Cr in 2025) — seller-favorable pricing likely.
Civil construction is cyclical, receivables-heavy, and dependent on government payment cycles.
red_flags: FY2025 OCF -36 Cr and FCF -58 Cr despite reported net profit of INR 25 Cr — earnings quality gap.
Total assets jumped 84% (239→440 Cr) in the IPO year — execution risk on deployed capital.
No dividend history disclosed — fails my preference for demonstrated cash returns.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the surface, B.R.Goyal is more disciplined than most recent listings. At INR 124, it trades at 8.44x earnings and roughly 1.1x book (Equity INR 245 Cr vs Market Cap INR 270 Cr), and the Graham Number using EPS ~11.5 and BVPS ~112 comes to ~INR 170 — so the stock technically sits below intrinsic. Borrowings at INR 77 Cr against Equity of INR 245 Cr yield a D/E of 0.31, and interest coverage (EBITDA 48 / Finance Cost 9) is a comfortable 5.3x. Revenue and profits have expanded over six years, with net profit compounding 25.6%. These are the hallmarks of a company I would normally investigate further.

My hesitation is the quality of those earnings. FY2025 Operating Cash Flow collapsed to -INR 36 Cr and FCF to -INR 58 Cr while reported profit rose to INR 25 Cr — a classic receivables/WIP divergence in civil contracting. The 84% jump in total assets and near-doubling of equity via what appears to be a fresh issue means the per-share economics and float are untested. Civil construction is among the most cyclical, capital-intensive industries with notorious payment delays from government counterparties. Without a multi-year record as a listed entity, verifiable dividend history, and proof that this OCF deterioration is transitory rather than structural, I cannot commit capital. HOLD: monitor two more years of cash flow before buying.
